sources.title: A prospective observational study of lucid episodes in advanced dementia
sources.original_date_note: First-online date confirmed in publisher-indexed article history; issue citation retained separately.
sources.design: Prospective audiovisual observations; multi-informant validation; within-person baseline comparison
sources.population: Advanced dementia participants recruited from one 12-bed dementia hospice unit.
findings: Directly observed episodes included increased meaningful vocalizations; features varied between people.
limitations: Events cluster within three people; nine episodes are not nine independent participants.
Single hospice unit, limited demographic diversity, irregular observations and unequal follow-up restrict prevalence and generalisability.
Observation window was 08:00–18:00, so coverage was not continuous.
Non-English speech could not be coded for multilingual participants, including one with a lucid episode.
Physiological correlates remain a proposed research direction; this observational study does not establish a survival mechanism.

sources.title: Data-driven detection of lucid episodes in advanced dementia: Application of latent class analysis to observational data
sources.design: Exploratory latent class analysis of existing audiovisual coding; within-person model development and internal robustness checks
sources.research_question: Can coded communication patterns help detect within-person lucid episodes, and must class definitions be individualised?
sources.population: The three people with informant-validated lucid episodes in the original advanced-dementia hospice cohort; selected on prior episode validation.
analytical_methods: All episode-containing segments plus a random 20% of communicative segments were coded. Segments are repeated measurements, not independent people or episodes.
Pooled variable filtering, zero-inflation handling, binarisation and correlation screening reduced 68 variables to 14 presence/absence indicators.
Compared latent class counts and shared versus person-specific response probabilities using model-fit criteria, particularly BIC; interpreted classes as communication engagement levels.

Compared candidate high-engagement class against previous informant labels; individual models also used leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). Supplement implementation and fold isolation not independently audited.
findings: Three-class unconstrained model had lowest BIC among the compared pooled/grouped solutions; sharing class response probabilities worsened BIC. One individually fitted case preferred four classes, but three were retained for comparison.

The high-engagement class contained most previously validated lucid segments; published main-analysis sensitivity ranged from 53% to 100% and specificity from 56% to 97% across three cases. These are segment-label comparisons, not independently validated clinical accuracy.
The analysis provides a candidate way to screen observed communication changes while preserving personal baselines; it adds no independent replication cohort.
limitations: Only three previously positive cases from one hospice setting; outcome-based selection excludes the other cohort members and limits transportability and prevalence inference.

Only suspected episodes underwent informant validation. The comparison negative category includes unreviewed segments; specificity and apparent false positives do not use a fully verified reference standard.
Repeated segments share individuals, days and episodes. LOOCV is internal validation; without supplement/code audit, temporal separation and nesting of variable selection remain unverified.

Presence/absence encoding discards intensity and segment duration; more speech or longer segments can affect indicators. Reported continuous, duration-normalised sensitivity analyses do not establish external validity.
Class labels are interpretations of behavioural clusters. A high-engagement segment is not automatically a validated lucid episode; some validated episodes need not have much speech.
No preregistration. Complete supplement, uncertainty estimates, reproducible code and independent external validation remain review requirements.
No neural measurements or test of post-mortem survival is established by this behavioural analysis; mechanism and consciousness claims remain hypotheses.
